PullRequest.Title: list: report list changes requested while rendering an element
PullRequest.Body:
%23%23 What

`ListView` now reports when a renderer callback (`renderElement` / `disposeElement`) causes the list itself to change:

- a `splice`
- an `updateElementHeight`
- a render, e.g. from a scroll or layout

The report is a `BugIndicatingError` passed to `onUnexpectedError`, so it lands in the renderer log with the stack that caused it, and in error telemetry. The message names the change and the renderer template, e.g.:

> ListView: 'splice' was requested from 'renderElement(session-item)'. Changing a list while it renders or disposes an element can leave stale rows in the DOM; defer the change until the list has finished rendering.

It reports **once per list instance** and changes no behaviour. It's a diagnostic, not a guard.

%23%23 Why

The Agents window sessions list showed overlapping, duplicated rows, and the renderer log had no errors at all. In a local repro, a row renders and reads an observable whose first subscription updates session state. The sessions list reacts right away and calls `tree.setChildren`, which splices the list view while it's still placing rows. This leaves stale rows in the DOM and throws nothing:

- `ListView` only rejects recursive splices ("Can't run recursive splices.").
- It doesn't catch a splice or height update from inside `render()`, or a height update from inside `_splice()`.

A hard guard isn't the right fix here. By the time the list view sees the change, the tree model and list traits have already moved on, so throwing can't undo it. Queueing the change would leave the model ahead of the view. This PR only makes the problem visible, so the next occurrence tells us which code triggered it.

%23%23 Notes for reviewers

- **Dynamic-height lists are excluded** (`supportDynamicHeights`). They support changes while elements render to be measured (%23330967, and the existing re-entrant tests in `listView.test.ts`).
- **Hot path:** the only cost per rendered or disposed row is setting and restoring one field around the renderer call.
- **Test impact:** the unit-test harness fails on unexpected errors, so any existing test that hits this path would now fail. I ran all `browser` (20,302) and `electron-browser` (2,109) unit tests with this change: nothing reported, no failures. I also replayed the sessions-list scenario, and it reports `'splice' was requested from 'renderElement(session-item)'`.
- **Telemetry:** if some list does this routinely in production, it will show up in error telemetry (once per list instance), which is what this PR is for.

%23%23 Tests

`listView.test.ts`: a splice requested from `renderElement` during a scroll, and a height update requested from `disposeElement` during a splice. Both are reported, once per list.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The scroll call path is explicit: `onScroll` calls `render`, which calls `insertItemInDOM`/`removeItemFromDOM` for rows crossing the viewport, and the added template literals execute directly before each renderer callback. The reporter explicitly returns for dynamic-height lists, proving these allocations are unused there. Exact frame-time magnitude depends on row churn and renderer cost, so severity is low rather than the mechanism being uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: short-lived diagnostic string objects and their interpolation CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One label allocation per row render and, when present, one per row disposal; cost grows with rows crossing the viewport during scrolling and with visible rows replaced by splices, rerenders, or layout changes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased CPU/GC pressure on list rendering and scrolling
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Renderer callbacks were invoked directly, so ordinary rendering, disposal, and scrolling did not construct callback-name strings or retain callback tracking state.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every rendered or disposed row now eagerly constructs a diagnostic label and assigns/restores callback state, even though almost all callbacks never trigger a report and `supportDynamicHeights` lists can never report one.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1056 newly evaluates `renderElement(${item.templateId})` before every `renderer.renderElement` call; the same added interpolation appears for each disposal at lines 671 and 1136.
Findings.Title: Build renderer labels only when a violation is reported
Findings.Impact: Rapid scrolling or replacing visible rows in long lists now creates avoidable short-lived strings on the rendering critical path, increasing allocation/GC pressure and the chance of scroll jank; chat and notebook dynamic-height lists pay the cost even though this diagnostic is disabled for them.
Findings.Evidence: `ListView` is the virtual scrolling engine. `onScroll` invokes `render`; the render-range loops invoke `insertItemInDOM` and `removeItemFromDOM` once for each row entering/leaving the viewport. The added wrappers eagerly interpolate `item.templateId` into fresh `renderElement(...)` / `disposeElement(...)` strings. Over a traversal of R rows this adds about R render-label allocations plus up to R disposal-label allocations, and viewport replacement/splice work scales similarly with the affected visible rows. `reportChangeDuringRendererCallback` normally returns because there is no nested change, and always returns when `supportDynamicHeights` is true, yet the labels have already been allocated. Dynamic-height consumers include chat and notebook lists.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the callback kind and template id without formatting (for example, separate primitive fields) and construct the human-readable label only inside the first reporting branch. Also bypass tracking entirely for dynamic-height lists and once `didReportChangeDuringRendererCallback` is set, while preserving nested callback restoration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial rendering, scrolling, and visible-row replacement in standard virtual lists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `onScroll` synchronously calls `render`, which removes and inserts viewport rows and invokes renderer callbacks before the frame can complete. The newly formatted callback labels are therefore on the scrolling/rendering critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is rows crossing the viewport: traversing R distinct rows creates roughly R render labels and up to R disposal labels; replacing a viewport scales with its visible row count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All row rendering and disposal is serialized on the browser UI thread; there is no limiter or parallelism. A viewport transition processes each entering/leaving row in its render loops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Diagnostic state is per ListView instance: the first violation sets `didReportChangeDuringRendererCallback`, but callback labels continue to be constructed afterward; ordinary and dynamic-height rendering receive no cached label or bypass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added template literals execute immediately before each row renderer callback, and the scroll-to-render call flow and per-row loops are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact allocation/GC cost depends on scroll distance, row height, renderer cost, and template-id length. The per-row allocation and synchronous critical-path reachability are certain, but DOM renderer work may dominate in many lists, supporting low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity regression: the diff adds eager short-lived string allocation per row on a global UI hot path, although labels are only consumed on the rare first nested change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling dynamic-height chat and notebook lists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A scroll event synchronously performs the standard render and then `_rerender` height reconciliation before the viewport update completes. Added labels in `insertItemInDOM` and `removeItemFromDOM` are on this UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible and newly exposed chat messages, notebook cells, settings rows, or profile rows; cost grows with row churn over the session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Height reconciliation and row churn are serialized on the UI thread; each affected row is processed sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dynamic-height measurements cache widths/heights per item, but the new callback-label work in normal insert/remove paths is not cached. The reporter always exits when `supportDynamicHeights` is true, so labels created by those paths cannot produce a report.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: chat and notebook enable `supportDynamicHeights`, while `reportChangeDuringRendererCallback` unconditionally returns for that option after the wrapper has already allocated its label.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dynamic-height consumers and the disabled-report condition are established; the number of row crossings and resulting GC impact varies with notebook/chat length and scrolling behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable as part of the same allocation finding because these important consumers pay per-row diagnostic allocation despite being categorically excluded from reporting.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A renderer-triggered splice, height update, or nested render constructs `BugIndicatingError` and synchronously invokes unexpected-error handling while the original renderer callback remains on the UI stack. Stack/message formatting and logging are on the critical path; the telemetry service's eventual emission is delayed and off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Formats and logs the captured error stack, then serializes/enqueues an error telemetry event for delayed emission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one diagnostic per ListView instance; telemetry coalesces equal buffered events before its delayed flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Renderer-requested list changes produced no unexpected-error log or telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unexpected-error message/stack formatting and `logger.error` invocation occur synchronously during rendering; telemetry transmission is deferred and does not block the current render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct ListView instances that encounter a renderer-induced list change, not number of rows or repeated violations within one instance.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Violation handling is synchronous and serialized with rendering. Telemetry events are buffered and flushed after five seconds rather than emitted concurrently per row.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The diagnostic is negatively coalesced only per list instance by `didReportChangeDuringRendererCallback`; separate lists can each report once. Error telemetry deduplicates equal events in a five-second buffer before flushing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous handler and delayed telemetry paths; lower magnitude concern because they run only after an actual renderer-induced list mutation and once per instance.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The known triggering pattern is realistic, but repository-wide prevalence and logger backend latency are unknown. Once-per-instance coalescing bounds the cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the synchronous work is bounded to one report per affected list and is the intentional diagnostic behavior; the delayed telemetry boundary is coalesced and off the render critical path.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced standard and dynamic-height list rendering, scroll/splice row churn, unexpected-error logging, and buffered telemetry. Submitted one low-severity allocation/GC finding for eagerly formatted per-row callback labels; no regression-fix learning signal applies.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
